name: Axfoundation
roleSummary: Swedish do-tank linked to Axel Johnson group. Operates Framtidens mat programme: develops circular feed (mycoprotein, insects, mussels), underutilized fish products, perennial grains, and side-stream food innovation.
currentRelevance: Launched world's first commercially sold fish raised on mycoprotein feed (2025). Over 300 partners and 100+ researchers. Model for how a trade-linked foundation can drive food system transformation.
notes: Funded by Axel Johnson/Antonia Ax:son Johnson family. Key programmes: Framtidens foder for fagel fisk och flask (2023-2026 with SLU), Smart Svensk Sjomat, Sillenbergare, Svensk baljvaxtfars. CEO: Maria Smith. Torsaker gard as living lab.

name: Roal Oy / AB Enzymes Finland
roleSummary: Finnish enzyme producer (part of AB Enzymes / Associated British Foods). Produces phytase, xylanase and other feed enzymes that enable circular feed formulations by unlocking nutrients in plant by-products.
currentRelevance: Factory expansion in Rajamaki (2024) specifically for feed enzyme production. Feed enzymes are a critical enabler for replacing fishmeal/soy with side-stream ingredients in Nordic aquaculture.
notes: Founded as Alko/Rohm JV. Over 90% of production exported. Key person: Dr. Kari Juntunen (Senior Research Scientist). Historical VTT collaboration. Feed enzyme market described as strongly growing.

name: Raisio Oyj
roleSummary: Finnish oat and feed group (Benecol, Elovena, Harkis). Developed Baltic Blend circular fish feed from Baltic Sea fish, reducing nitrogen emissions by 75%. Collaborates with Nordic Umami Company on side-stream upcycling.
currentRelevance: Sold Raisioaqua to Alltech/Finnforel (2023) for aquaculture gigafactory. Still active in plant protein (Harkis fava bean) and side-stream valorization (oat husks to energy, fava shells to umami sauce).
notes: Baltic Blend uses recycled nutrients from Baltic Sea. Green Deal signatory for plastic reduction. Oat husk-fired plant for carbon neutrality. Partnership with Nordic Umami Company for waste-to-taste.

name: Nordic Umami Company
roleSummary: Finnish food-tech that transforms food industry side-streams into fermented umami ingredients using microbial processes. Partners with Raisio on fava bean shell and oat residue valorization.
currentRelevance: Active commercial partnership with Raisio producing umami sauce from production waste. Represents the waste-to-taste approach to side-stream upcycling in Nordic food systems.
notes: Uses microbial fermentation to convert low-value side-streams to high-value ingredients. Collaboration with Raisio documented in 2024 press release.

name: Volare
roleSummary: Finnish insect protein startup producing black soldier fly protein from food industry side-streams. Spun out of VTT LaunchPad. Building dedicated protein factory (Volare 01).
currentRelevance: Secured EUR 26M funding for new factory. Part of VTT deep-tech incubator ecosystem alongside Enifer. Represents Finnish insect protein sector distinct from Norwegian players.
notes: VTT LaunchPad spinout. EUR 26M secured for Volare 01 factory. Focuses on BSF larvae fed on food industry side-streams.

name: Finnforel Oy
roleSummary: Finnish RAS aquaculture innovator building a circular trout gigafactory. Acquired Raisioaqua feed production with Alltech to vertically integrate circular feed into land-based fish farming.
currentRelevance: Joint venture with Alltech (2023) positions them as integrated circular aquaculture company: own feed production + RAS farming. Explicitly marketed as circular economy model.
notes: Partnered with Alltech (global feed expertise). Acquired Raisioaqua feed factory. Positioning as aquaculture gigafactory with circular economy branding.

name: Pronofa AS
roleSummary: Norwegian alternative protein company in Fredrikstad aiming to produce 50,000 tonnes of insect larvae per year for feed. Acquired Ecoprot. Part of MultiFuelLarve research consortium.
currentRelevance: Most ambitious insect protein scale-up in Norway. Target of 50,000 t/yr would make it one of Europe's largest. Previously pursuing stock exchange listing.
notes: Headquartered in Fredrikstad. Ambition 50,000 t larvae/year. Acquired Ecoprot. Consortium member with Invertapro, Norinsect in MultiFuelLarve project.

name: Norinsect AS
roleSummary: Norwegian insect company producing mealworm larvae for feed and food. Commercial production with ambition for multiple facilities in Norway. Part of MultiFuelLarve research consortium.
currentRelevance: Active commercial producer complementing BSF-focused peers (Invertapro, Pronofa). Mealworm specialization differentiates from black soldier fly players.
notes: Mealworm larvae focus (vs BSF for Invertapro). MultiFuelLarve consortium member. Plans for multiple Norwegian production facilities.

name: Ecoprot AS
roleSummary: Norwegian insect larvae producer and project lead for MultiFuelLarve research project converting organic waste to valuable larval products. Now part of Pronofa.
currentRelevance: Key R&D actor documenting safe use of various organic waste fractions as insect feed substrate. MultiFuelLarve project (with NIBIO, Invertapro, Pronofa, Norinsect) is Norway's largest insect research consortium.
notes: Acquired by Pronofa. Project lead MultiFuelLarve. Focus on documenting regulatory pathways for using organic waste streams as insect substrate.

name: BIO3 AS
roleSummary: Norwegian company licensing Enifer's PEKILO mycoprotein technology to build a mycoprotein factory in Norway for the salmon feed industry. Factory planned from Q3 2025.
currentRelevance: Bridge between Finnish biotech (Enifer) and Norwegian salmon feed market. If successful, provides domestic alternative to imported soy protein concentrate for aquaculture.
notes: Licensed Enifer's Pekilo technology January 2025. Factory planned Q3 2025. Targets Norwegian salmon feed industry specifically.

name: Mycorena AB (BANKRUPT - acquired by Naplasol)
roleSummary: Swedish mycoprotein startup (Promyc brand) producing fungal protein as B2B ingredient. Founded 2017 in Gothenburg by Ramkumar Nair. Went bankrupt 2024, acquired by Naplasol/VEOS Group.
currentRelevance: Key Nordic alt-protein failure case. ~300 MSEK invested. Failed Series B in tight funding market. IP and platform now continuing under Belgian industrial owner Naplasol.
notes: BANKRUPT 2024. Total ~300 MSEK raised. Failed Series B 2022-23. B2B customers (plant-meat brands) slowed growth plans. Acquired by Naplasol (VEOS Group, Belgium). IP continues under new owner.

name: Hooked Foods AB (BANKRUPT)
roleSummary: Swedish plant-based seafood startup. Founded 2018 by Tom Johansson. Produced vegan fish products for retail. Filed for bankruptcy 2026 after seven years.
currentRelevance: Nordic alt-seafood failure case. Over 6 MUSD raised. Revenue ~1.4-1.86 MSEK with -6.2 MSEK loss in final year. Only 3 employees at bankruptcy. Illustrates difficulty of plant-based seafood category.
notes: BANKRUPT 2026. Over 6 MUSD raised over 7 years. Weak market response, tight margins, limited control over value chain. Production was contract-based (co-packing). IP status unclear.

name: DUG Foodtech AB (BANKRUPT)
roleSummary: Swedish potato-based milk alternative (formerly Veg of Lund). Stock-listed. Declared bankrupt December 2025 despite distribution in REWE, Lidl, Rossmann.
currentRelevance: Alt-dairy failure case despite strong distribution (Germany, Sweden). Multiple failed emissions and refinancing attempts. Patent on potato emulsion technology is key IP in bankruptcy estate.
notes: BANKRUPT 19.12.2025. Listed on Swedish exchange. Multiple capital raises failed to achieve profitability. Had distribution in REWE, Rossmann, Kaufland (DE) and Lidl (SE). IP (potato emulsion patent) open for acquisition.

name: Ynsect (BANKRUPT)
roleSummary: French insect protein producer (mealworm-based). Founded 2011 by Antoine Hubert. Was world's most capitalized insect startup with >500 MUSD raised. Entered judicial liquidation 2025.
currentRelevance: Global insect sector's biggest failure. Despite massive funding, could not reach break-even on industrial mealworm production. Pilot plant near Dole acquired by founder's new company Keprea.
notes: BANKRUPT 2025 (judicial liquidation). >500 MUSD raised. Entered safeguard 2024, reorganization 2025, then liquidation. Could not finance continuation plan despite strong IP. Some assets acquired by Keprea (Antoine Hubert).

name: Infarm (RESTRUCTURED)
roleSummary: Berlin-based vertical farming company. Founded 2013 by Erez and Guy Galonska and Osnat Michaeli. Raised ~500 MUSD, reached unicorn valuation. EU operations collapsed 2023, restarted as Infarm Technologies Ltd.
currentRelevance: Most spectacular vertical farming failure in Europe. ~1000 employees at peak. Energy crisis and operational inefficiency made European indoor farming unviable. Pivoted to single factory in Canada (kosher niche).
notes: RESTRUCTURED 2023. ~500 MUSD raised, unicorn at peak. EU insolvency, assets bought for ~40M EUR (IP valued at 1 EUR). Now Infarm Technologies Ltd focused on Canada. Cited energy crisis and operational inefficiency.

name: Meatless Farm (BANKRUPT - brand acquired by VFC)
roleSummary: UK plant-based meat brand founded 2016 by Danish entrepreneur Morten Toft Bech. Entered administration 2023. Brand and some rights acquired by VFC.
currentRelevance: Plant-meat winter casualty. Raised tens of millions GBP. Could not weather downturn in plant-based meat demand combined with tough macroeconomics. Brand continues under VFC.
notes: BANKRUPT/administration 2023. Founded by Danish Morten Toft Bech. Over 100 employees at peak. Plant-meat category fatigue + funding freeze. Brand acquired by VFC.

name: Solar Foods Oy
roleSummary: Finnish food-tech producing Solein protein from CO2, water and electricity via gas fermentation. Represents the e-protein/power-to-food approach to circular protein production.
currentRelevance: Relevant as CCU case in food systems: uses CO2 as carbon source for microbial protein. Referenced in CCS/CCU analysis as example of synthetic food from captured carbon. Novel Food approval process ongoing.
notes: Uses CO2 + water + electricity to produce protein via hydrogen-oxidizing bacteria. Factory 1 built. Novel Food approval process in EU. Volumes still small vs industrial CCS. Not permanent carbon removal.

name: VermiNord
roleSummary: Norwegian vermicompost developer using cold earthworm composting to convert organic residuals into soil amendments. Three-step process: pretreatment, worm composting, quality monitoring.
currentRelevance: Represents decentralized, low-tech biorest innovation outside large waste companies. Challenges: Nordic frost, limited volume capacity per area vs. biogas/thermal composting.
notes: Small-to-medium scale. Cold vermicomposting with epigeic earthworms. Regulatory: sale as fertilizer requires Mattilsynet registration. Key challenge is climate (frost) and low volume capacity.

name: Bokashi Norge
roleSummary: Norwegian B2C company selling bokashi equipment, starter cultures and courses for household/neighborhood-scale lactic acid fermentation of food waste. Used as case in Circular Regions.
currentRelevance: Represents decentralized, urban circular food waste treatment model. Regulatory challenge: no heat hygienization makes scaling to commercial fertilizer product difficult under current Mattilsynet rules.
notes: Business model: equipment/culture sales (B2C), courses, consulting. Circular Regions case study. Key barrier: lack of heat treatment prevents scaling to professional commercial fertilizer. R8 positioning.

name: Naplasol (VEOS Group)
roleSummary: Belgian biomass fermentation company in VEOS Group. Acquired bankrupt Mycorena's IP and mycoprotein platform (2024), integrating Promyc technology into industrial fermentation portfolio.
currentRelevance: Industrial acquirer of Nordic alt-protein IP. Represents pattern where traditional ingredient companies absorb failed startup technology. VEOS Group has fermentation infrastructure and market access that startups lacked.
notes: Part of VEOS Group (Belgium). Acquired Mycorena's bankruptcy estate August 2024. Has existing fermentation infrastructure. Promyc mycoprotein IP continues under industrial ownership.

name: Oatly AB
roleSummary: Swedish oat milk company and largest Nordic plant-based dairy brand. Major generator of havre-okara (oat residue) side-stream estimated at hundreds of thousands of tonnes wet mass annually across Nordic operations.
currentRelevance: Relevant as both side-stream generator (okara to feed/biogas) and as survivor in alt-dairy category where DUG failed. Stronger brand and distribution scale differentiate from bankrupted peers.
notes: Listed company. Major okara side-stream generator. Internal work on okara utilization in new ingredients. Survived alt-dairy shakeout due to brand strength and distribution scale. Cost-cutting mode post-2022.

name: Biomega
roleSummary: Norwegian company processing salmon by-products using enzymatic hydrolysis into high-value protein and oil. Represents marine side-stream upgrading from feed-grade to food/nutraceutical grade.
currentRelevance: Active in transforming fish processing waste into higher-value products. Technology potentially relevant for broader side-stream valorization in Nordic seafood sector.
notes: Enzymatic processing of fresh marine by-products. Produces protein hydrolysates and marine oils. Documented in FHF (Norwegian Seafood Research Fund) project database.

name: HOFF SA
roleSummary: Norwegian potato processing cooperative (pommes frites, chips, frozen). Major generator of potato peel and trim side-streams estimated at several kilotonnes per factory per year.
currentRelevance: Key Nordic potato side-stream holder. No dedicated PeelPioneers-type valorization exists in Nordics; most goes to feed/biogas. Potential for fiber/starch ingredient extraction.
notes: Potato peel/trim waste is one of 13 most promising side-streams identified in Danish industry mapping (DI Fodevarer). Nordic potato waste currently goes mainly to animal feed and biogas. No Nordic PeelPioneers equivalent exists.

name: PeelPioneers
roleSummary: Dutch company extracting oils, fibers and bioactive components from citrus peels before the energy/compost step. Benchmark for Nordic vegetable-rest upgrading that does not yet exist in the region.
currentRelevance: Referenced as the model that Nordic actors lack. No equivalent company identified in Nordics for fruit/vegetable peel valorization to specialty ingredients. Demonstrates the gap.
notes: European benchmark for citrus peel upcycling. Extracts essential oils, dietary fiber, d-limonene from orange peels. No Nordic clone identified in 2022-2026 research.

name: Alvdalslax
roleSummary: Swedish rainbow trout farm partnering with Axfoundation on Framtidens fisk - world's first commercially sold fish raised on mycoprotein-based circular feed (replacing soy and fishmeal).
currentRelevance: Commercial partner in Axfoundation's breakthrough circular feed project. Fish sold in Hemkop and Urban Deli (2025). Demonstrates that circular aquaculture feed can reach retail shelves.
notes: Partner in Framtidens foder project (SLU + Axfoundation). Rainbow trout raised on mycoprotein, insects and mussels. Sold commercially in Hemkop/Urban Deli 2025.

name: Northern Lights JV
roleSummary: CO2 transport and storage joint venture (Equinor, Shell, TotalEnergies) as part of Norway's Longship CCS project. Will store Yara's 800,000 t CO2/year from Sluiskil from 2026.
currentRelevance: Critical infrastructure for food system decarbonization via Yara partnership. Connects fertilizer production to permanent geological CO2 storage. Cost ~1150-1280 NOK/tonne CO2.
notes: Part of Longship. Aurora reservoir in North Sea. Explicitly NOT for EOR. Yara binding commercial agreement 2023. Cost estimates ~1150 NOK/t CO2 (2024). Capacity expandable.

name: Innovafeed
roleSummary: French insect protein company (BSF) that survives where Ynsect and ENORM failed. More gradual scaling, selective high-value markets (petfood first), and stronger industrial backing.
currentRelevance: Key survivor in European insect sector. Contrasts with bankrupt peers through modular capacity building, conservative CAPEX approach, and petfood-first commercial strategy rather than megafactory model.
notes: Survived insect sector shakeout 2023-2025 where Ynsect and ENORM failed. Differentiated by: modular scaling (not megafactory), petfood focus for higher margins, industrial partnerships.
